summary: The prepared main revision already removes the synchronous GPU Tensor.tolist() calls from EAGLE verification. run_eagle_verify returns device tensors, and GenerationBatchResult.copy_to_cpu stages token IDs and accept lengths into pinned host buffers with nonblocking D2H. A regression test verifies the source invariant and the real gfx950 copy path for empty and multi-request results. No additional runtime correction was justified.

tests.what_was_measured: Three tests passed: no cpu/tolist/numpy conversion in run_eagle_verify; pinned asynchronous device-to-host copies preserve multi-request token IDs and accept lengths on gfx950; zero-length results are handled correctly.

The reported v0.5.12 implementation contains synchronous accept_index.tolist(), predict.tolist(), num_correct_drafts_cpu.tolist(), and num_accept_tokens_cpu.tolist() calls in EagleVerifyInput.verify, establishing that the regression would fail on the reported source.
The assigned device is one AMD Instinct MI355X, gfx950, unique ID 0x91222c17f0f648d7.

gpu_execution.evidence: The regression executed real ROCm tensor creation, nonblocking GPU-to-pinned-host copies, CUDA/HIP event synchronization, and exact host-value comparison on HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 (gfx950).

remaining_limitations: The reported GLM-5.1 FP8 weights were unavailable.
The assigned environment has one gfx950 AMD GPU, not eight H200 GPUs, so TP8, CUDA/H200 behavior, 80K-160K prompts, near-full KV pressure, and the original watchdog hang were not reproduced.
The test qualifies the corrected EAGLE result-transfer boundary and transport values only; it does not qualify GLM-5.1 model semantics or a distributed workload.

On HIP, the scheduler currently performs this pinned asynchronous copy on the forward stream by design; the regression verifies absence of Python-side Tensor.tolist() in run_eagle_verify and correct pinned D2H, not CUDA copy-stream overlap.
